name: How Do I Verify a Kitchen Contractor’s Measurements Before Ordering Custom Cabinets?

mainEntity.name: What measurements should I verify before approving custom kitchen cabinets for a San Diego remodel?
mainEntity.text: What measurements should I verify before approving custom kitchen cabinets for a San Diego remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Custom cabinets should be based on a coordinated field measure, not a quick wall-to-wall estimate. Verify finished floor height, ceiling and soffit dimensions, wall plumb, corner angles, window and door trim, casing depth, appliance openings, utility locations, and obstructions. Record the location and height of every outlet, switch, shutoff, drain, gas line, vent, and duct. Measurements taken before demolition may change once drywall, flooring, or old cabinets are removed. Ask for a second verification after the work area is exposed and before cabinets are fabricated. Confirm whether dimensions include finished materials, backsplash thickness, filler pieces, end panels, crown, light rails, and appliance panels. Review shop drawings showing plan, elevations, sections, hardware, fillers, panels, and appliance clearances. Make sure the contractor identifies who owns measurement responsibility and what happens if approved drawings conflict with site conditions. Do not approve fabrication while critical appliance specifications or utility locations remain uncertain. A careful verification process helps prevent crooked installations, unusable fillers, countertop rework, and schedule delays.
acceptedAnswer.description: Verify room length and width, ceiling height, wall plumb, corner angles, window and door dimensions, finished-floor height, appliance sizes, plumbing locations, outlet positions, and obstructions such as beams or vents. Confirm measurements after demolition when conditions are visible, and approve scaled shop drawings before fabrication.
